טֶרֶם is rendered by the whole not yet. Head on yet, which carries the temporal lexeme; the competing head is not, on the reasoning that heads a Nor on its negative (rule 35).
Finite verb with its copular auxiliary and phrasal particle, discontinuous around the negative under rule 25; out completes the lexeme of gone out (rule 44).
Participial predicate with the construction-supplied copula and the phrasal particle of laid down (rules 20, 44).

The italic to sleep answers to no morpheme: laid down has already written שָׁכַב's lexeme, and the sleeping is nowhere in the clause (rule 44). The two words stand together and do one office, so they are one added unit (rule 2).

The relative and the resumptive adverb שָׁם share the single where (rules 22, 30), headed on the relative. The verbless clause's copula joins that unit because שָׁם is the clause's predicate and its sense stands inside the fused word; the unit is discontinuous under rule 25. Competing reading: put was on the subject אֲרוֹן, but rule 20 sends the copula to the predicate.

review_notes: The ASV's italics on to sleep corroborate the added unit and do not decide it (rule 7).
שָׁם is a resumptive adverb inside the where fusion rather than an unrendered occurrence (rule 22).
